_meta.purpose: Per-SKU DTC product cost (COGS) + full retail price. Consumed by Module A (attribution & unit-economics) to compute contribution margin per order.
_meta.cost_source: Raphael's canonical COGS = gebeauty/boxes/'Estudo estoque 2026 apresentacao (1).xlsx' -> Planilha1 'Preco minimo'. That study adds +R$2,00/unit of B2B/wholesale handling ('Considerei R$ 2,00'); for DTC we STRIP that R$2. So unit_cost_brl = study 'Preco minimo' MINUS 2.00. Verified 2026-07-22: every SKU below reconciles exactly to study-minus-2.
_meta.retail_source: Shopify list price (productType=product), full-size retail. Campaign prices differ.
_meta.cost_confirmed: Lucas 2026-07-22 (CORRECTS the 2026-07-21 note): unit_cost_brl is the LANDED product cost - it ALREADY INCLUDES inbound freight, import/duty and breakage/loss (not formula+packaging only). Therefore the Module A 1.48x COGS plug is RETIRED (params.cogs_calibration_factor=1.0) and COGS is now pure bottom-up. Still modeled SEPARATELY (not in this number): outbound delivery/freight-to-customer, fulfillment/pick-pack, payment fees, tax. This is STEP 1 of a bottom-up build; shrinkage, seeding/gifting and expiry write-offs beyond per-unit breakage will be added later as explicit lines, not a plug.
caveats: GEB 008 (Shampoo a seco) is NOT in this study sheet; its R$11.21 is from an earlier source and is UNVERIFIED against the current study basis (Lucas 2026-07-22: keep as-is for now).
Landed cost per unit; excludes only the downstream cost-to-serve (delivery, fulfillment, payment, tax) which live in params.json.
Retail = full list; realized price per order comes from Shopify lineItem discountedTotal at run time.
